Where the implant goes is decided on a screen first.
At the Tysons Corner office every implant starts as a cone-beam scan: the jaw in three dimensions, with bone volume and nerve position measured before surgery rather than discovered during it.
The scan becomes a printed guide, so the implant lands at the planned angle and depth, with smaller incisions and a shorter recovery.
One specialist owns all three steps
: Dr. Nahlah plans the implant, places it and makes the tooth that sits on it.
Four visits to a finished implant.
Time with Dr. Nahlah, a cone-beam scan and an examination. You leave knowing whether you are a candidate, what it costs and how long it will take.
If a tooth has to come out or bone has to be rebuilt, that happens first; grafting brings several months of healing before the implant.
Often a few hours, through the guide made from your scan, with nitrous oxide or oral sedation. Most people are back to normal activity within a week, eating soft food while the implant fuses.
About four months later, once bone has grown onto the post, the final crown, bridge or arch is attached, matched to your shade and bite.

Does Dr. Nahlah place the implants himself?
Yes. He plans the implant on the scan, places it and restores it, so the tooth on top is designed by the person who chose where the post went.
Can I be sedated for implant surgery in McLean?
Yes: nitrous oxide, or oral sedation if you would rather be more relaxed. After oral sedation you need someone to drive you both ways.

How long will my implant take?
From a few months to over a year. The implant itself fuses in about four months; extractions or bone grafting beforehand add their own healing time.
Is there a warranty on implants?
Yes, five years on implant procedures, kept by coming in for a cleaning every six months.
